_doc: PRE-REGISTERED candidate list for the STRUCTURE-STOP (chart-stop-primary) exit validation study. Frozen BEFORE any candidate replay is run (ground rule: exploratory != confirmatory -- no re-picks after seeing results; FAIL is publishable). Motivated by 2026-07-09: three fleet round-trips premium-stopped on the 747.46-reclaim signal while SPY never printed a 5m CLOSE below 747.46 -- a close-below-trigger structure stop would have held all three. Today is EXHIBIT-ONLY and is excluded from every population used for pass/fail (it generated the hypothesis; testing on it would be circular).

CONTROL.label: shipped -20%/+150%/sell80/fixed premium-only shape (no structure stop, ever)

SS-A.label: structure stop primary + -50% catastrophe cap + TP1 +150% sell66 + runner trail 15%

structure_stop.rule: calls: exit ALL on first 5m SPY CLOSE strictly below trigger_level; puts: first 5m CLOSE strictly above trigger_level

SS-C.label: SS-A with a $0.10 buffer on the structure-stop trigger

structure_stop.rule: calls: exit ALL on first 5m CLOSE strictly below (trigger_level - 0.10); puts: first 5m CLOSE strictly above (trigger_level + 0.10)

c6_fill_mark_convention.statement: The structure stop evaluates only CLOSED 5m SPY bars -- a bar's close is knowable only once the bar ends. This study fires the structure-stop exit at the NEXT bar's OPEN premium (not the close-bar's own closing premium), applied uniformly to SS-A/SS-B/SS-C, both layers, and the exhibit. Rationale: the breach is only knowable at the close-bar's end (== the next bar's start), so a same-bar-close fill would assume execution at a price that was not yet actionable; the next bar's open is the first tradeable premium after the signal is knowable. Within any single bar, the structure-stop-due check is evaluated BEFORE the ordinary touch-based checks (catastrophe stop / TP1 / trail / time stop) for that same bar, because a due structure-stop exit is decided at the bar's open, logically before any of that bar's intrabar movement can be realized.

layer_a_fresh_slice.method: tw8_level_context.enrich_signals() -- EXACT trigger-bar identification via a tight-tolerance close-price match against the signal's own entry_spot field (both values originate from the same source CSV), then detect_level_reclaim/detect_level_rejection against the per-day-frozen level set (lib/levels.py._detect_from_history, orchestrator's exact convention).

layer_b_anchor_and_exhibit.method: Real fleet fills carry no entry_spot label (unlike the simulator signal schema), so the exact-match method above is not available. Instead: derive side from the option symbol (OCC format SPY{YYMMDD}{C|P}{strike}), convert entry_ts_utc to ET, compute the date's frozen level set (same lib/levels.py convention), then scan SPY 5m bars with timestamp_et <= entry_ts_et backward from the CLOSEST bar to entry (most recent first) for the first bar where detect_level_reclaim (calls) / detect_level_rejection (puts) fires against the frozen level set. Returns the first (closest-to-entry) hit.
layer_b_anchor_and_exhibit.lookback_rationale: Generous ceiling for order-placement + confirmation-bar lag between the true trigger bar and the fill timestamp (disclosed heuristic, not exact -- real fills do not carry the simulator's entry_spot label needed for exact-match recovery).
layer_b_anchor_and_exhibit.precision: approximate (backward-scan heuristic within a bounded lookback window)
layer_b_anchor_and_exhibit.expected_gap_vs_live_engine: lib/levels.py._detect_from_history is a DISCLOSED APPROXIMATION of the production level-writing process (its own module docstring: 'In production, levels are written by premarket from chart structure + protocol audit. For backtest, we approximate from price history alone.'). It also does NOT model the level-memory system (G11 level-memory-live-merge, wired 2026-07-09, automation/state/key-levels.json 'level_memory' source) -- so a recovered level near-but-not-identical to a live-engine-reported level (e.g. the task's cited 747.46) is EXPECTED, not a bug. This gap is pre-existing and disclosed, not introduced by this study.

fallback_rule.statement: A position/signal whose trigger_level cannot be recovered (no_level_set / no_bars_before_entry / no_trigger_bar_in_lookback / trigger_bar_unmatched) is NEVER dropped. It is replayed under the SAME candidate shape with the structure-stop check disabled (ss_time forced to None) -- i.e. it falls back to the -50% premium catastrophe cap + TP1 + runner trail only, exactly as CONTROL and any other premium-only replay would treat it. This satisfies the pre-registered pass-bar condition 3 by construction.
does_not_apply_to: CONTROL (never has a structure-stop layer, trigger_level or not)

time_stops.disclosure: This 10-minute asymmetry between layers is PRE-EXISTING in the codebase (T5/T-W8 already carry it) and is preserved here for consistency with prior work, not introduced by this study.

option_bar_granularity.spy_bars_both_layers: 5-minute SPY bars, ET, via tw8_level_context.load_spy_full (cached CSV through 2026-07-08) + a live yfinance fetch appended for 2026-07-09 (read-only; not written to backtest/data/ or any production cache).

pass_bar.statement: ALL three conditions must hold for a candidate (SS-A/SS-B/SS-C) to PASS:
pass_bar.condition_1_layer_b: beats CONTROL total on layer (b) real-fills anchor -- interpreted as STRICTLY GREATER THAN (a tie is not a beat).
pass_bar.condition_2_layer_a: beats CONTROL expectancy on layer (a) fresh slice -- interpreted as STRICTLY GREATER THAN.
pass_bar.condition_3_fallback: positions/signals without a recoverable trigger_level are included under the disclosed fallback (premium-only -50% cap), never dropped -- a structural/methodology invariant, verified true by construction and by test, not a per-candidate numeric outcome.
pass_bar.aggregation: AND of all three -- ANY failing condition fails the candidate. No partial credit.
pass_bar.today_exhibit_excluded: The 2026-07-09 exhibit table plays NO role in any pass/fail verdict -- it is shown for narrative context only, clearly labeled EXHIBIT ONLY.

no_repick_clause: Once this file is frozen, no candidate shape, buffer, lookback window, time-stop, or fill-mark convention may be edited in light of results. A FAIL is a publishable, informative outcome, not a reason to adjust the pre-registration and re-run.
